title: A stored boosted_h past timedelta's range raises in the boost restore task on every restart
claim: boost._restore_settle builds timedelta(hours=boosted_h) for any finite non-negative boosted_h, and store.ABSURD (1e15) admits values far past timedelta's range, so for 4 of 5 stored values (3e10, 1e11, 1e12, 1e14 h) the restore task the coordinator spawns raises OverflowError on both of two restarts (8 of 10), leaving the running space overlay's start (space_since) unrestored and the boosted time at timedelta(0) instead of the 'unknown' (None) the loader's own comment prescribes; the fifth (1e10 h) loads as ~47 000 years.
mechanism: The guard `isinstance(hours, (int, float)) and 0.0 <= hours < math.inf` accepts any finite hours; held.space_settle_until is set before the timedelta call, so the raise leaves a half-applied restore and skips the space since/end handling below it; the exception escapes the spawned restore_session task (Home Assistant logs 'Task exception was never retrieved' each start). The document is not rewritten by the failed restore, so the same failure recurs at every restart until a later boost overwrites the store. DOMAINS declares the field `space_settle/boosted_h: _Z0`, which only the debug-level off-domain diagnostic reads.

evidence.unit: restarts (of 10: 5 values x 2 restarts on the same document) whose boost restore task raises
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

instrumented_symbol: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/boost.py:_restore_settle (via the coordinator constructor's spawn_restore_session -> restore_session -> restore, on a real loop; boost.held_for state read back)

perturbation.change: --fix: _restore_settle treats a boosted_h at or past timedelta.max in hours as unreadable (None), its docstring's rule for an unreadable value; patched in memory

metric_definition: Restarts whose spawned boost restore task raises, over 5 out-of-range boosted_h values x 2 restarts on an unchanged document.
phenomenon_property: Every stored duration a loader turns into a timedelta is bounded to what its writer can produce (or read as unknown) before conversion, so no stored number below store.ABSURD can raise out of a restore.
seam_rule: grep -nE 'timedelta\((hours|minutes|seconds|days)=' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  (those whose argument comes from a stored document; store_fuzz.py's 'huge' operator drives them per store)

null_control.note: RESULT control_restarts_raising: the same record with boosted_h=1.5 restores space_since and 1:30:00 on both restarts

reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/store_fuzz.py --stores boost   -> boost_task_raise=3 (op=huge on space_settle/boosted_h)
proposed_fix_scope: boost.py:_restore_settle bounds boosted_h (e.g. to the settle tail's own maximum) before timedelta(); a corrupt value reads as unknown.
